eligibility.evidence: Sections 2-3 (pp. 1-4): gpt-3.5-turbo is given relation-extraction and intent-detection benchmarks (TACRED, Banking77, MASSIVE, GoEmotions, 20 Newsgroups) with labels shuffled; label-order bias is called 'primacy effect' and Asch 1946 is cited, but no cognitive-experimental task or human-study item is administered. Reviewer could count the cited primacy bias as the paradigm.

G.notes: Borderline on E2: the primacy label is borrowed from Asch (1946) to name a label-position bias in NLU classification; no human comparison and no cognitive task. Referee would ask whether any classic serial-position or order-effect paradigm was adapted. Only gpt-3.5-turbo (temperature 0.0) tested.
